text:
Sam (sales): Heads up — Acme POC is failing during demo prep. Client uploads a conversation archive (~2.8MB) as base64 in the payload and our API returns 413 Payload Too Large. Demo tomorrow AM, need a short-term workaround. :grimacing:

Mira (eng): Which endpoint? hosted or dedicated? Can you paste headers + a curl example?

Sam (sales): Hosted, POST /v1/chat. Here's a minimal repro they used from the browser (they base64 attachments into `messages[*].meta`):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-infer-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"...","meta":{"attachments":"<base64 big blob>"}}]}'
```

Response: `HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large` with no helpful body.

Toni (eng-ml): Short answer: our hosted ingress (Cloud LB) has a ~2MB default body limit for JSON payloads. Big base64 blobs blow past that. Two practical workarounds for a short demo: gzip the body (Content-Encoding: gzip) or avoid embedding binaries — upload to storage and send a pointer.

Mira (eng): Quick patch to try now: client-side gzip + Content-Encoding header. Many HTTP clients and node fetch variants support this. Example server-acceptable curl: 

```
# create gzipped payload first
echo '{"model":"gpt-infer-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"...","meta":{"attachments":"<base64>"}}]}' | gzip -c > payload.gz
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" \
  --data-binary @payload.gz
```
Mira (eng): If the browser client can't gzip easily, use multipart/form-data streaming or upload the file to S3 (pre-signed) and pass `attachment_url` in the JSON. Backend can fetch the file and stitch text into the context.

Sam (sales): Browser-only customer — pre-signed S3 upload might be simplest. Any security concerns about fetching from random S3 URLs?

Julie (solutions): We recommend pre-signed URLs scoped to a short TTL, and the ingestion service verifies the content type/size before pulling. For enterprise customers, we can also accept an S3 object + signed manifest and perform server-side validation. :white_check_mark:

Toni (eng-ml): Also note billing: we bill on tokens produced from text we process. If attachments are just stored as blobs and not text-extracted, they don't count as tokens. If we OCR/extract text from attachments, that extracted text will be tokenized and billed. Good to clarify with Acme.

Sam (sales): Quick triage plan for demo: 1) try gzip approach with a small demo artifact; 2) if browser cannot gzip, implement pre-signed upload + `attachment_url` path; 3) follow up with infra for ingress limit increase if they want to continue embedding.

infra-bot: Created infra request INFR-1234 to evaluate increasing hosted ingress JSON body limit and associated risks.

Mira (eng): For longer-term: we shouldn't accept arbitrary base64 payloads in JSON. We'll publish a short doc recommending streaming / presigned upload patterns and add a server-side rejection message with guidance instead of generic 413. I'll draft the doc and drop a link here when ready.

Sam (sales): Thanks all. I'll circle back to Acme with the S3 approach and demo fallback. If you can drop the doc link, I can include it in the email to their engineering contact. :pray:
